name: Liquid hydrogen
principle: Hydrogen is cooled to about -253 °C in a liquefier using precooling and a hydrogen or helium refrigeration cycle, with ortho-para conversion catalysts so the liquid does not boil off from conversion heat. The liquid is stored and shipped in vacuum-insulated tanks and regasified at the user.

advantages: Highest gravimetric density of any carrier
Used commercially for decades in merchant gas supply
limitations: Liquefaction consumes a large share of the hydrogen's energy
Boil-off losses during storage and shipping
Very large LH2 carriers are not yet built
